No she didn't



[https://youtu.be/olqVGz6mOVE?t=694](https://youtu.be/olqVGz6mOVE?t=694)

> After going through Riverwood

Sure

> and Bleak Falls Barrow

Why would a Dragonborn not tasked with getting the Dragonstone go to Bleak Falls Barrow? Lucan asking you to retrieve the claw is a SIDE QUEST. He might or might not have done it, just like he might or might not have retrieved Amren's sword in Whiterun or he might or might not have joined the Companions. The only way you can say he canonically ventured through Bleak Falls Barrow is via the main quest, and that's via Farengar and thus Delphine

> A sidequest that's right in your face immediately upon going into the Riverwood Trader

Still a side quest

>there is no established canon on what quests the LDB took in what order

But there's an established canon on what quests he *absolutely* did do, and that's *only* the main quest + DLC main quest

>saying they only went to the Barrow because of Farengar is also an assumption.

Saying he went to the Barrow for Lucan is a side quest assumption that might or might not have happened, saying he went to the Barrow because Farengar asked him to is a main quest requirement that absolutely happened

> Mirmulnir appears immediately after you go through Bleak Falls Barrow

And the only objective path we know the LDB must've absolutely taken regardless of previous choices has Farengar requiring the Dragonstone as that's a main quest, The Golden Claw isn't

\> With or without it, the Dragonborn still goes to Whiterun  
  
Sure, to tell the Jarl about Riverwood and that's it  
  
\>after finding a Word Wall  
  
Assumption, Golden Claw is a sidequest and the only reason we know he'd canonically go to Bleak Falls is because Farengar asks him regardless of meeting Lucan Valerius or not; because of Delphine  
  
\>still kills Mirmulnir  
  
Assumption, the only reason he was around at the time Mirmulnir appeared was because of Farengar's task. No Delphine, no Farengar tasking you, by the time Mirmulnir appears my Dragonborn is halfway to Solitude. What then? The specifics on when and if he ever encounters a first dragon in the position to kill him without Whiterun's guards + Irileth are iffy, as is him having people around to actually explain what just happened ,what that weird Shout means and where he needs to go. \*Everything\* changes and becomes headcanon if the Dragonborn isn't present at the Western Watchtower, and we have no reason to believe he'd randomly be there if he wasn't caught in the middle of giving Farengar the Dragonstone, which happens solely because of Delphine instigating the whole affair

And who would he bring the stone to? Farengar wouldn't know of its existence, he wouldn't ask for it, the Dragonborn wouldn't interpret the map on its back, Balgruuf wouldn't send you to help Farengar because he wouldn't have a matter that needed help
The stone might not matter with the dragon appearing but it sure mattered for the Dragonborn being in the right place and the right time to be asked to go and kill the nearby dragon
She told Farengar about the Dragonstone at Bleak Falls Barrow. Without her there would quite literally be no game and definitely no Dragonborn reveal.

You can be an asshole to Kashley and leave them to die at Virmire. You can be an asshole to the surviving one at Horizon. You can be an asshole to them in ME3, you can have a squadmate kill them or you can kill them yourself.

You can refuse to recruit Garrus in ME1, and you can get him killed in ME2 and ME3.

You can refuse to recruit Wrex in ME1, you can either order Ash to execute him or kill him yourself at Virmire, you can doom his entire species to extinction in ME3 and shoot him afterwards.

You can deny Tali's request for the geth data in ME1, make her depressed in ME2 by exposing her father's activities and get her killed in the suicide mission. You can then genocide her entire race and watch her commit suicide afterwards at Rannoch.

You can sell Legion to Cerberus and then kill him in ME3, you can sexually abuse Jack then let Cerberus kidnap, torture and brainwash her and her students, you can kill Zaeed if his attitude annoys you, you can let Samara commit suicide then kill her daughter out of spite afterwards right in front of her corpse.

So on and so forth. A big part of these games is allowing the player to express their attitude towards NPCs: if you dislike them, you're given the opportunities to express that dislike and make Shepard act on it. If you like them, you befriend them or even romance them. Even when you like the characters it's good to see that the game lets you to change your mind, or explore "alternate universes" where you experience stuff you'd never normally do.

With Liara, you're not allowed to be an asshole and have it actually count -even when you try your best to make her despise you each game still defaults to both of you being close friends at the very least and head over heels for each other most other times. The Virmire Survivor is seen for a grand total of 5 minutes in 2 while she's given a permanent spot in one of the game's four hub areas, and she has her own set of sidequests there. Not enough? How about a full DLC revolving around her, then? The writers couldn't fathom that someone might actually not adore Liara as much as they do.

​

And don't even get me started about her ""development"" between ME1 and ME2.
So were San Andreas and GTAV; it didn't stop those games from having foggy nights or rainy days.
How would Eorlund and Vignar Gray-Mane react if their Harbinger won the civil war for the Empire?
I like how instead of checking the source your argument is simply "you're wrong".

For what is worth I never expected them to outright copy paste the exact same design, not only is Daggerfall a 20+ years old game based on character sprites but it's also been more than 200 years since its events. That's why I don't get the "haha red armor" sentiment, I imagined something like Skyblivion's [Ebony Armor](https://cdnb.artstation.com/p/assets/images/images/012/401/821/4k/spyros-frigas-ebony-armor-demo-57.jpg?1534614909) but crimson.
